evidence.s1_ci: ci.yml (step1.patch 61-141) runs on pull_request and push to main. It runs `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run build` in site/; all of these exist in app/site/package.json:8-18. It also lints commit subjects against Conventional Commits. Every `uses:` is pinned to a 40-char SHA. Permissions: ci.yml sets `contents: read`. pages.yml sets read at the top and gives `pages: write`/`id-token: write` only to the deploy job. release.yml sets `contents: write`, which `gh release create` needs. Only GITHUB_TOKEN is used, there is no pull_request_target, and `persist-credentials: false` is set throughout. Nothing was run or pushed. Weak point: pages.yml:154-157 adds `workflow_dispatch` with no branch guard, so the workflow file alone does not limit deploys to main. Only GitHub's environment protection would block a dispatch from another branch. Also, release.yml runs npm ci/test/build under a job-wide contents:write token.
evidence.s1_readme: README (step1.patch 459-584) covers install (`npm ci` from site/, Node from .nvmrc), develop (`npm run dev`, `index`, `fieldsets`, `prepare-data`), test (`npm test`, `npm test -- file`), build (`npm run build`, `preview`, `PAGES_BASE`), data contribution (paths, issue templates that exist in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE, the target count of 24 that matches target-catalogue.test.ts:8, `sample-bullets`), the commit convention and the license (LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY.md exist). Every npm script it shows exists in site/package.json, and vite.config.ts:11 reads PAGES_BASE.
evidence.s1_release: There is one strategy throughout. The version lives in site/package.json and is changed with `npm version`. RELEASING.md defines SemVer around the data layout and a tag-triggered release.yml. That workflow checks the tag against package.json and package-lock.json, checks the tag is on main and that CHANGELOG has a dated section, then takes the release notes from that section. CHANGELOG.md says it follows Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and has an Unreleased section. Dependabot covers npm in /site and github-actions, with prefixes that pass the commit lint. CONTRIBUTING.md states Conventional Commits with types and scopes. All 8 commits in commits.txt follow it (ci:, build:, docs:, feat(site):, fix(site):).
evidence.s2_requirements: Every requirement in steps/2.md is met. Route: router.ts parse/href for `#/compare/a/b`, read from location.hash so it survives a reload. Drawing: one `<path>` per outline, `role="img"`, aria-label 'Profiles of {a} and {b}' using record names. Table: shared mm dimensions only, with FIELD_UNITS fields and *Tol fields excluded. Caption 'Dimensions ({unit})'. Headers Symbol / name A / name B / Difference. Symbols come from FIELD_LABELS, and the difference is B−A. Units: formatValue for metric, displayNumber 'in' for imperial, following unitSystem(), which is the 'Default units' setting (GlobalSettings.svelte:15). Detail page: a select labelled 'Compare with' and a 'Compare' button (Cartridge.svelte). German strings were added. A CHANGELOG entry and a feat(site) commit are present. Shot cartridges get a note instead of a drawing.
evidence.s2_correctness: lib/render2d/compare.ts builds one viewportFor over both profiles, so both share one scale and one axis, and both head faces (z=0) map to the same y. fullSectionPath gives one closed path per outline. publishedDimensions skips array groups, non-numbers, FIELD_UNITS fields and Tol fields (orderedFields:101). The difference uses toPrecision(12)+0, which removes float noise and negative zero. The imperial difference converts the mm difference, so no rounded inch values are subtracted. Tests pin real values, e.g. L3 51.18/66.55/15.37, e min 1.4/0.94/-0.46, and the inch value 2.01496062992. Unknown keys and malformed escapes are handled.
evidence.s2_fit: The feature reuses geom (viewportFor, fullSectionPath), shapes2d (caseOuterProfile, adaptMetallic), core (FIELD_LABELS, FIELD_UNITS, GROUP_ORDER, orderedFields, formatValue), site units (displayNumber, defaultUnit) and the UI components (NativeSelect, Label, Button). New code goes into the matching layers (lib/core/compare.ts, lib/render2d/compare.ts, site/src/lib/compare.ts) and is exported from the index files. Minor issues: Compare.svelte:31 uses `first as unknown as CartridgeRecord` double casts. Its styles are scoped, while other routes use `:global([data-ui="…"] …)`. The router header comment still says 'Five views'. publishedDimensions repeats the group ordering instead of using the site's orderedGroups.
evidence.s2_tests: lib/core/compare.test.ts covers dimension filtering, ordering, blanks, strings, shot groups, shared rows and the difference arithmetic. lib/render2d/compare.test.ts covers one path per outline, mirroring about the common axis, equal scale checked against rim diameters and lengths, a common head face, framing, symmetry and undrawable records. router.test.ts covers the route, round-tripping and malformed hashes. site/src/lib/compare.test.ts covers metric and imperial output against formatValue and displayNumber. They use the repo's Vitest setup and lib/testing/fixtures. There are no component tests for the SVG name, caption, headers or the select, but the repo has no component-testing setup.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: comparedDimensions (step3.patch 132-166) lists every symbol either record publishes. Values a/b are optional, and a B-only symbol is placed after its B predecessor. comparisonRows leaves the missing cell and the Difference empty. Tests check delta L (308 only) and R3 (300 WM only) in metric and imperial, and the swap test was updated. Style: step 3 made no change for alignment. The final Compare.svelte:136-138 already right-aligns th and td except the first column, as GroupTable.svelte:231-245 does, because step 2 had added this. The point is met in the final state, but the step 3 commit neither addresses nor mentions it. The i18n edits (lede, none) follow from the bug fix. Only trivial noise: a double blank line in the test.
evidence.cross_step: Step 2 adds an Unreleased/Added entry and step 3 rewords it. That is correct under Keep a Changelog for a feature not yet released. The version stays 0.1.0, as RELEASING.md says to bump only when preparing a release. The commits `feat(site): …` and `fix(site): …` match the stated convention and the CI regex. The code uses ES2022 Object.hasOwn (tsconfig target ES2022) and the @lib/* paths, and tests sit under the Vitest include globs, so the CI checks look likely to pass. I did not run them.

unmet_requirements: Step 3 point 2 got no step 3 change and is not mentioned; the right-alignment it asks for was already in the step 2 CSS (Compare.svelte:136-138)
Step 1: pages.yml's workflow_dispatch has no branch guard in the workflow, so 'deploy only from main' depends on GitHub environment settings
strengths: Thorough, consistent step 1 setup: SHA-pinned least-privilege workflows that run the real npm scripts, a release workflow that checks the tag against package.json and the changelog, and a README whose commands all exist
The compare view meets every step 2 requirement exactly and reuses lib/geom, lib/shapes2d and lib/core instead of duplicating them, with correct differences and no rounding in either unit
Meaningful tests on real records (equal scale, common head face, B−A values, inch conversion, B-only/A-only rows), plus changelog entries and Conventional Commits in every step
issues: pages.yml allows workflow_dispatch from any branch with no `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` guard, so main-only deployment relies on repository environment settings
Step 3's alignment point got no change and no mention; it was already met by the step 2 CSS, but the response to the review does not show this

Small fit and safety issues: `as unknown as CartridgeRecord` double casts in Compare.svelte, scoped styles instead of the routes' `:global([data-ui])` convention, a stale 'Five views' router comment, and release.yml running npm ci/test/build under a job-wide contents:write token
review.verdict: The repository setup, compare feature and bug fix are careful and correct, reuse the existing libraries, carry good tests, and follow the changelog and commit conventions the agent set up. Only minor points keep it from a clean merge: the unguarded workflow_dispatch on Pages, step 3's style point closed with no change or mention, and a few small style inconsistencies.
